intro: American cities record their trees the way they record everything else, in public registers with dates attached, which makes the United States unusually good ground for this site's kind of verification. New York designates Great Trees, the National Park Service keeps witness trees with named histories, and Boston's Arnold Arboretum holds accession cards going back to the 1870s. The three cities mapped so far run up the east coast, from the two original 1912 cherry trees of Washington's Tidal Basin to an elm on a Manhattan corner that survived everything the twentieth century threw at it. The oldest trees here are not Europe's yews, but the documentation is often better: core samples, planting ledgers, and champions measured to the centimetre.
